proposed_capability: P95 + Trifecta P08/P82/P07: extend the existing opt-in hover-learning semantic-event port to catalog-qualified hotkey and Sims cheat invocations. Capture structured canonical action references and optional later independently reviewed outcomes; project the same 3/5/10/30/60-minute behavior windows by channel. No raw keylogging, cheat command text/arguments, global hooks, autonomous game input, new learner or background polling.
player_save_control_impact: Only opt-in semantic action observations from already active host_listener sessions; never intercept broad keyboard activity, store raw console commands or amounts, install hooks, or take input. Existing player-first and 15-second game-action admission stay untouched.
expected_outcome: Existing hover behavior evaluator supports canonical hotkey_action and cheat_action events with unique interaction_ref, validated against owning ui-chrome and game-cheat contracts, safe event-time counts and independently reviewed outcome rates without crediting invocation as effectiveness.
negative_tests: Unknown mode/hotkey and unrecognized cheat IDs rejected
Raw keystrokes, typed command, cheat parameters and unsanitized names rejected
Duplicate events/interactions or unmatched outcomes rejected across channels
A hotkey request is not evidence mode changed
Cheat submission is not evidence of game effect
Mixed tooltip/hotkey/cheat patterns isolated and counted without inflation
Active listener opt-in, writer bounds and no game input preserved
Five time windows and review-only thresholds hold
Exact-game P08 proof not inferred from synthetic tests
rollback_path: Revert feature PR; existing tooltip-only event format remains compatible. Per-session event sidecars are ignored by Git and never migrate personal game data.
unresolved_unknowns: Actual Sims 4 key/console callback exposure and exact game patch calibration are unavailable from GitHub; live game cannot be certified here
Additional recognized command families must be added through owning catalogs rather than arbitrary text capture
